For the Storyteller: how the farmer, the dog and the kid hunt for turkeys, how to set the difficulty, and three farms ready to play.

You are the Storyteller. You run the farmer, the farm dog, the farmer’s kid and the farm. You don’t decide where the farmer goes or whom he finds: the dice and the farm’s tables do that. What you decide is how he sounds. Make him loud, cheerful, determined and a little bit clumsy. He is not a villain. He just really, really wants a turkey.

Your job

  • Set up the farm and the clock (Chapter 12 has a checklist).
  • Keep the round moving. Let the turkeys plan, then nudge them along: if a turn drags, count down from ten in your best farmer voice. Each player says what their own turkey does.
  • Run the farmer’s turn exactly as below, and roll in the open so everyone sees the dice.
  • Ham it up. Talk to the turkeys you can’t see. Sniff the air. Peer into the hayloft. Then roll.
  • Rule fairly. If something comes up that the book doesn’t cover, pick the answer that’s funnier and kinder to the flock, and keep playing.

The farmer’s turn

In round 1 the farmer is indoors pulling on his boots: skip his turn entirely (and the dog’s, and the kid’s). For the whole of round 1 they don’t count for anything (Chapter 3), and Hazel’s Keen Eye has nothing to see. From round 2’s turkeys’ turn on, they count as usual. From round 2 on, do these steps in order. “The farmer’s turn” always means all six steps, the dog’s and the kid’s included.

1. Grab

First, any Spotted turkey that isn’t in his zone stops being Spotted: he’s lost sight of it. Then, if a Spotted turkey is in the farmer’s zone, he grabs it and the game ends: the flock loses. If several Spotted turkeys are there, he grabs the one with the highest urge (if they’re tied, the lowest card number). If a decoy is ready (Chapter 6), he grabs that instead, carries it to the Farmhouse (move him there), the clock moves down 2, and you skip steps 2 to 4. Every turkey he had Spotted there goes free: his arms are full. The dog and the kid still take their steps.

2. Walk

Check these in order, and do the first one that applies:

  1. Detour. If a detour prank went off since his last turn, put him straight in that prank’s zone (if two did, the one that went off first; the other waits for his next turn). He’s busy there: skip the search (step 3), but take any “Huh?” tokens in that zone off the map. Go on to step 4.
  2. Rake. If he stepped on a rake (a farm event), he doesn’t walk this turn. (A detour still moves him, and the rake is used up.)
  3. A “Huh?” token. If there’s a token anywhere on the farm, he heads for the nearest one (the fewest paths away; if two are equally near, the newest; if they went down at the same moment, you pick). Use the numbered tokens in order, so the highest number out is always the newest. When you need a token and the next number is already on the map, take the tokens on the map and renumber them from 1 in the same order. If all 20 are down, use a coin: it’s the newest until the farmer clears it. He walks along the shortest way, up to 2 zones (3 on Hard), and stops as soon as he’s in the token’s zone. Where two ways are equally short, he takes the first-listed path (in the farm table’s “Paths to” column) in each zone where the ways split. A token in his own zone means he stays put and searches.
  4. His route. Otherwise, roll a d6 and read his zone’s route line in the farm table: he walks to that zone. (If Hazel’s Keen Eye has already rolled it this round, use that roll. If the oven has preheated, roll again from his new zone and walk a second zone.)

3. Search

  • Every turkey in the open in his zone is Spotted. (Only the zone he ends in: he doesn’t spot anyone in zones he walks through.)
  • If there are “Huh?” tokens in his zone, he checks every spot they’re on. A token on the zone itself (not on a spot) means he rolls his zone’s search line for a spot as well.
  • If there are no tokens in his zone, roll a d6 on his zone’s search line: he checks that one spot.
  • After the whole family helps look (a farm event), he checks every spot in the zone this turn.
  • Every turkey in a spot he checks rolls to stay hidden, target the spot’s cover, one at a time in any order the flock likes. Boosts work as usual, and the flock can spend a Feather on a gobble. If the roll fails, or it gobbles (he’s right there), that turkey is Spotted.
  • Then take every “Huh?” token in his zone off the map.

4. Close Calls

Every turkey in his zone that isn’t Spotted raises its urge by 1. Two things change this: no Close Calls in Hazel’s zone (Keen Eye), and a Scaredy turkey has one from next door too.

5. The dog

Only on Standard and Hard. The dog starts in the Farmhouse. Roll a d6.

  • 1–2 (1–3 on Hard): it follows its nose one zone toward the nearest turkey (the lowest card number if two are equally near; the first-listed path if two ways are equally short). If that turkey is in its zone already, it stays.
  • Otherwise, roll again and read its zone’s route line, and send it there.
  • Every turkey in the dog’s zone that isn’t Spotted rolls 4+ to stay hidden, whatever its spot, even in the open. A turkey that fails gets barked at: a “Huh?” token on its spot (or the zone, if it’s in the open). The dog never grabs and never makes anyone Spotted itself (a gobble on its roll is still an ordinary gobble).
  • Turkeys in the dog’s zone have a Close Call, unless the farmer already gave them one this turn.

6. The kid

Only with 5 or more turkeys. The farmer’s kid starts in the Farmhouse.

  • Roll a d6 on its zone’s route line and move it there.
  • If any turkey is in the open there, the kid yells “DAD! TURKEY!”: a “Huh?” token on the zone.
  • Roll the zone’s search line: the kid peeks into that spot. Each turkey in it rolls the spot’s cover; if anyone fails, a “Huh?” token goes on that spot.
  • The kid never grabs, never makes anyone Spotted itself (a gobble on its roll is still an ordinary gobble), and causes no Close Calls.

The end of the round

After the farmer’s turn: move the Dinner Clock down 1 (if it reaches 0, the flock wins; if it lands on an EVENT space, roll the farm event), then every turkey that isn’t Spotted raises its urge by 1, and Pip rolls for his hiccups.

Farm events

Roll on this table whenever the Dinner Clock lands on or jumps past an EVENT space (every multiple of 4). An effect “on his next turn” lasts for one farmer’s turn. A farm event is its own thing: its urge change applies even if a turkey’s urge has just risen for something else, and so do the quirks it sets off. An event rolled during the farmer’s turn (from the decoy’s clock jump) affects his following turn.

d6EventWhat happens
1The truck backfiresBANG! Every turkey’s urge rises by 1.
2Grandma callsThe farmer goes straight to the Farmhouse to answer it. Move him there now.
3The whole family helps lookOn his next turn, the farmer checks every hiding spot in the zone he ends in.
4He steps on a rakeTHWACK. On his next turn, the farmer doesn’t walk (he still searches his zone).
5A cold gustEvery turkey fluffs up and huddles down: every turkey’s urge falls by 1.
6The oven is preheatedDING! On his next turn, if the farmer walks his route, he hurries: roll his route die twice and walk two zones.

Things the farmer says

  • “Heeere, turkey turkey turkey!”
  • “I know you’re in here. I can smell the nervousness.”
  • “Was that a gobble? That was definitely a gobble.”
  • “Biscuit! Find the turkey! No, not the squirrel! Biscuit!”
  • “Who tipped over my milk pails?!”
  • “Gobble back if you can hear me!” (Nobody ever does.)

Questions that come up

Does the farmer chase a token he walks past?

He heads for the nearest token and stops when he reaches its zone. Tokens in zones he only walks through stay where they are for later.

A turkey moved away from its token. What now?

He goes there anyway and checks the empty spot. That’s the point of moving away.

What if a spot is full?

Nobody else can hide there. If no spot in a zone has room, a turkey in that zone is in the open.

Can a turkey walk into the farmer’s zone?

Yes, with a 4+ Sneak roll (fail it and you’re Spotted on the spot). It’s cleverer than it looks: on his turn he walks off before he searches, unless a “Huh?” token is in his own zone or he’s stepped on a rake. Hiding right behind the farmer is very brave and very funny.

A detour and a “Huh?” token at the same time?

The detour wins: he goes to the detour zone. Tokens elsewhere wait for his next turn.

The clock hits 0 while a turkey is Spotted?

Too Late beats everything. The flock wins.

Can the flock give up?

No. Turkeys never give up. (If the table really has to stop early, call it a draw and eat some pie, but never to dodge a grab.)

Before you start, pick a difficulty and count your turkeys. Together they set where the Dinner Clock starts, how many Feathers the flock gets, and who helps the farmer look.

Difficulty

DifficultyThe dogThe farmerClockFeathersThe flock wins
EasyStays indoorsRuns 2 zones to a “Huh?” token−4+1about 9 games in 10 (nearer 8 in 10 with five or more turkeys)
StandardFollows its nose on 1–2Runs 2 zones to a “Huh?” token——about 4 games in 5
HardFollows its nose on 1–3Runs 3 zones to a “Huh?” token, and Scram needs 5++2−1about 3 games in 5

The last column comes from playing tens of thousands of games by these rules with a computer, with a sensible flock that pranks when it’s safe and hides when it isn’t. A bolder or more careful flock will do a little better or worse, and a flock that learns to lead the farmer around with “Huh?” tokens will win more often. That’s the game working. If your table gets too good at it, move up a difficulty.

  • Easy is for a first game, young players, or a table that wants to laugh more than sweat.
  • Standard is the game as intended: you’ll usually win, and you’ll nearly always have a scare.
  • Hard is for experienced flocks. Expect to lose a turkey quite often, and expect it to be dramatic.

Where the clock starts

The Dinner Clock starts at 16, plus 1 for every turkey. A small flock of 2 or 3 turkeys takes 2 off; Easy takes 4 off, Hard adds 2; and each farm has its own small adjustment (Puddlewick +1, Windy Ridge +1). This table has done the sums for Bramble Farm:

Feathers

The flock starts with 2 Feathers. A small flock (2 or 3 turkeys) gets 1 more. Easy gives 1 more; Hard takes 1 away.

Big flocks: the farmer’s kid

With 5 or more turkeys, the farmer’s kid comes out to help (Chapter 7). A big flock has more friends to save each other and more beaks for pranks; the kid keeps it honest.

Small flocks

A flock of 2 or 3 turkeys gets the shorter clock and the extra Feather above. With only 2 turkeys there’s just one friend to save you, so every Spotted moment matters: with 2 turkeys, Hard wins only about half the time.

How long a game takes

A game lasts about 8 to 13 rounds. Allow about a minute for each turkey and two for the farmer every round, plus 15 minutes to set up and learn:

To play faster with a big flock, give everyone ten seconds to choose, or play on Easy.

Choosing a farm

  • Bramble Farm (Chapter 9): the friendliest map, best for a first game.
  • Puddlewick Farm (Chapter 10): split by a creek, with chokepoints; best with 4 or more turkeys.
  • Windy Ridge Farm (Chapter 11): open hillsides where the farmer gets everywhere fast; for flocks that have played before.

Bramble Farm sits at the end of a bumpy lane: a red barn, a white farmhouse, a duck pond, and more pumpkins than anyone needs. It’s the best farm for a first game: everything is close together, the paths are easy to follow, and the hiding spots are generous.

The farmer and the dog

Farmer Bramble is big, cheerful and very proud of his prize pumpkin. He wears a hat with earflaps and talks to himself the whole time (“Now where would I hide, if I were a turkey?”). Biscuit is a golden farm dog who loves everyone, especially squirrels.

The pranks

  • Turn off the oven. Sneak into the kitchen and peck the big knob back to OFF. Nobody notices for ages, and the oven has to warm up all over again.
  • Let the cows out. Lift the latch on the pasture gate. Daisy, Buttercup and Mabel go for a stroll, and the farmer has to herd them back.
  • Wake the rooster. Reginald the rooster crows at the top of his lungs. Very loud. Very funny. Very easy to find.
  • Dress the scarecrow as a turkey. Feathers, a paper snood and a sign saying “TURKEY”. The farmer falls for it, once.
  • Tip over the milk pails. SPLOOSH. Milk everywhere, and a lot of mopping.
  • Let down the tractor tires. Pssssssst. Now he has to walk everywhere, and find the pump.
  • Untie the rowboat. It drifts gently out into the pond. The farmer wades in after it, muttering.
  • Roll the giant pumpkin. The prize pumpkin goes bouncing down the hill. Everyone on the farm hears it go.

Playing Bramble Farm

  • Clock adjustment: none (use Chapter 8’s table as it is).
  • The Barnyard in the middle is open ground: crossing it is quick, but nobody can hide there.
  • The Cornfield rows hold six turkeys at 3+: the best group hiding spot on the farm, and the dog’s favorite place to sniff.
  • The oven is in the Farmhouse, where the farmer and the dog start. It’s the biggest prank, and the hardest to reach while he’s at home.

Puddlewick Farm is wet. A creek runs right through the middle of it, and the only ways across are the old footbridge and a splashy ford by the duck pond. There’s a water mill, a greenhouse full of tomatoes, a goat called Old Gertie who has opinions, and mud. So much mud.

The farmer and the dog

Farmer Puddlewick wears bright yellow waders all year round and squelches wherever he goes. Pickles is a very long, very low dachshund with a very good nose.

The pranks

  • Hide the roasting pan. No pan, no roast. It’s under the porch swing now, probably.
  • Let the goats loose. Old Gertie leads a daring escape, and the farmer spends his whole turn chasing goats.
  • Start a hen party. Twenty hens, all talking at once. The noise carries across the creek.
  • Turn on the sprinklers. Every sprinkler in the greenhouse goes off at once. The farmer runs in to turn them off and comes out soaked.
  • Jam the water wheel. A well-placed stick, and the mill grinds to a halt. That’s going to take a while to fix.
  • Gobble up the pie berries. No berries, no pie. Grandma will be furious, and the farmer has to go and pick more.
  • Start the duck choir. Quack. QUACK. QUAAAACK. Very loud, very out of tune.
  • Dress a hay bale as a turkey. Two pinecone eyes and a red sock for a snood. It’s not great, but it only has to work once.

Playing Puddlewick Farm

  • Clock adjustment: the clock starts 1 higher than Chapter 8’s table says.
  • The creek cuts the farm in two. North of it there are only two ways back: the Footbridge and the ford at the Duck Pond. Don’t get stuck on the wrong side.
  • The Berry Patch is a dead end: one path in, one path out, the same one.
  • The Muddy Lane is open ground in the middle of everything.
  • Puddlewick is a little kinder to big flocks and harder on small ones: with only 2 turkeys, play it on Easy or Standard.

Windy Ridge Farm is perched on a hilltop where the wind never stops. There’s a creaky windmill, a meadow full of sheep, a pigsty, and great open slopes where a turkey can be seen from a mile away. Every zone joins up with its neighbors, so the farmer can get anywhere fast.

The farmer and the dog

Farmer Windle is tall, cheerful and has been chasing his hat across this hilltop for thirty years. Moose is an enormous shaggy sheepdog who herds everything, including turkeys, chickens and occasionally the farmer.

The pranks

  • Unplug the oven. Pull the plug and push it behind the cupboard. It’ll be ages before anyone notices.
  • Send his hat up the windmill. Hook the farmer’s best hat onto a windmill sail. Up it goes. Round it goes. He has to get it back.
  • Stampede the sheep. One very loud gobble in the middle of the flock, and the sheep go everywhere.
  • Carve a pumpkin turkey. A big orange body, a stick neck, a pumpkin-leaf tail. From a distance, it’s a turkey.
  • Hide the tractor keys. Somewhere in the hay. Good luck, Farmer Windle.
  • Let the pigs loose. Eight muddy pigs, one gate. The farmer spends his turn chasing them round the yard.
  • Let down the truck tires. No truck, no trip to the store for a spare turkey.
  • Shake the apple trees. Apples everywhere, thumping on the ground like a drum.

Playing Windy Ridge Farm

  • Clock adjustment: the clock starts 1 higher than Chapter 8’s table says.
  • The Hilltop and the Driveway are open ground, and every zone has paths to all its neighbors: the farmer gets around quickly.
  • The Sheep Meadow has one huge spot, Among the sheep (3+, room for six). It’s noisy getting in, and the whole flock in one spot is a lot of turkeys for one bad roll.
  • The Pigsty is noisy too, and the pigs don’t mind sharing.

Never played before? This chapter gets you from an empty table to a farmer in his boots in about fifteen minutes. For a first game, play Bramble Farm on Easy with 3 to 5 turkeys.

What to print

  • The map of your farm (Chapter 9, 10 or 11), one copy for the middle of the table, and the farm table (the last pages of the same chapter) for the Storyteller.
  • A turkey card for each player (the sheets at the back).
  • The Dinner Clock sheet and the tokens sheet. Cut the tokens and turkey cards out before game night, or use coins and buttons for the tokens.
  • The At the Table sheet: one for every two players.
  • The Storyteller’s Card, for the Storyteller.

Everything works in black and white: nothing in this game is shown by color alone.

What you need

  • 3 white dice (action dice), 5 red dice (gobble dice), 1 helper die of a third color, and 1 die for the Storyteller. All are ordinary six-sided dice. If you have no red dice, any color that’s different from the white ones will do.
  • A coin or paperclip for each turkey’s urge, and a coin for the Dinner Clock.
  • A pencil for the prank boxes.

Setting up

  1. Choose a farm and a difficulty (Chapter 8).
  2. Lay out the map. Put the farmer in the Farmhouse. On Standard and Hard, put the dog there too. With 5 or more turkeys, the kid as well.
  3. Choose turkeys (Chapter 2). Each player takes the card and puts a coin on urge 1.
  4. Put every turkey in the Turkey house, in the Turkey Pen. They all start hidden.
  5. Set the Dinner Clock to its starting space (Chapter 8).
  6. Put the flock’s Feathers in the middle, where everyone can reach them (Chapter 8).
  7. Put the “Huh?” tokens and the decoy next to the Storyteller.
  8. Hand out the dice. They go round the table to whoever is rolling.
  9. Read the whole game in one breath (Chapter 1) out loud.
  10. Start round 1. The farmer is indoors pulling on his boots, so the flock gets a free turn to scatter.

Teaching it in five minutes

Say this

“It’s Thanksgiving, you’re turkeys, and the farmer wants one of you for dinner. If he grabs anyone, we all lose. If we stall him until this clock hits zero, it’s too late to cook, and we all win.

“Every round, each of you does one thing: sneak to the next zone, hunker down and calm down, pull a prank to waste his time, or gobble to save a friend. When you roll, the white die is what you’re trying to do; you need the target, like 4+. You also roll a red die for every point of your urge. Any red six and you gobble. Out loud, please. Gobbling tells the farmer where you are.

“If he finds you, you’re Spotted. You get one chance to run, and your friends get one chance to distract him, before he grabs you next turn. Feathers can swallow a gobble, but we don’t have many. Right: he’s putting his boots on. Scatter!”

Then teach everything else as it comes up. The At the Table sheet has it all on one page.

Example of play: the first three rounds

Setup. Bramble Farm, Easy, three turkeys: Pip, Duchess and Big Tom. The Dinner Clock starts on 13 and the flock has 4 Feathers.

Round 1. The farmer is indoors. Pip uses Soft Steps to Sneak two zones, through the Barnyard into the Pumpkin Patch, and hides in the Big pumpkins: with the farmer indoors and nothing Noisy on the way, there’s nothing to roll. Big Tom Sneaks into the Chicken Coop. It’s Noisy, so he rolls 3+: white 4, red 2. He hides Behind the coop. Duchess Hunkers Down in the Turkey house (urge 1 to 0).

End of the round: the clock moves to 12, an EVENT space. The event is a cold gust: everyone’s urge goes down 1 (as far as 0). Then everyone’s urge goes up 1, so all three are at 1. Pip rolls his hiccup die: a 3, no hiccup.

Round 2. The farmer is out on the porch now. Pip Pulls a Prank: Roll the giant pumpkin, 4+, one box. White 5, red 2. It works! The clock jumps from 12 to 9, and because the prank is loud, a “Huh?” token goes on the Pumpkin Patch.

Duchess wants out of the pen before the farmer looks there. The farmer is next door, so her Sneak to the Chicken Coop needs 4+: white 6, red 3. A Great: she can keep going one more zone, because a Sneak from the Coop to the Tractor Shed wouldn’t need a roll (the farmer isn’t in or next to either, and the shed isn’t Noisy). She hides Under the tarp, and then, being a Show-off, she strikes a pose: a second “Huh?” token goes on Under the tarp. Big Tom Hunkers Down (urge 1 to 0).

Farmer’s turn: nobody is Spotted, so no grab. There are two tokens, both three zones away, so he heads for the newer one, Duchess’s, two zones: Farmhouse to Turkey Pen (the first path listed) to Chicken Coop. He hasn’t reached it yet. There’s no token in the Coop, so the Storyteller rolls its search line: 2, the Nesting boxes. Empty. Big Tom, Behind the coop, has a Close Call (urge 0 to 1). End of the round: the clock moves to 8, another EVENT space. The event is “The whole family helps look”. Urges rise: Pip 2, Duchess 2, Big Tom 2. Pip’s hiccup die: a 5, phew.

Round 3. The farmer is in the Chicken Coop with Big Tom, and Duchess’s token is next door: next turn he’ll check every spot in the Tractor Shed. Duchess has to go. The farmer is next to the shed, so it’s a 4+ roll into the Noisy Duck Pond: white 5, red 2, 3. She slips into the Reeds.

Big Tom Sneaks out of the farmer’s own zone into the Big Barn, 4+: white 4, red 1, 6. He makes it to the Hayloft, but he gobbles. A token there would be just as near the farmer as Duchess’s old one, and newer, so he’d come straight to the barn. The flock spends a Feather (4 to 3): no gobble, no token. Pip, far away, Sneaks from the Pumpkin Patch to the Apple Orchard with nothing to roll and hides in the Leaf pile.

Farmer’s turn: the Tractor Shed token is one zone away and the Pumpkin Patch token three, so he goes to the shed and, with the whole family helping, checks every spot there. Both are empty. “Who’s been posing in my tractor shed?!” End of the round: the clock moves to 7. Urges rise: Pip 3, Duchess 3, Big Tom 3. Pip’s hiccup die: a 2. Everyone should Hunker Down soon, and the old token is still waiting in the Pumpkin Patch.

After the game

Win or lose, finish with the last word: the gobbled turkey’s famous last gobble (Chapter 5), or what’s for dinner instead (Chapter 6). Then swap Storytellers, pick another farm, and see you next Thanksgiving.

Every word the rules use in a special way, in one place. Each term means only this, everywhere in the book.

Action
What a turkey does on the turkeys’ turn: Sneak, Hunker Down, Pull a Prank, Gobble for a Friend, Scram or Let It Out. One per turkey per round (Chapter 3).
Boost
One extra white die on a roll: a knack, Lend a Wing or Puff Up. Never more than 3 white dice (Chapter 3).
Boxes
The tick boxes on a prank. A roll that works ticks one (a Great ticks two); when they’re all ticked, the prank happens (Chapter 6).
Close Call
The farmer (or the dog) ends his turn in your zone and you aren’t Spotted: +1 urge (Chapter 4).
Cover
The roll a hiding spot needs to stay hidden in it, from 3+ to 5+ (Chapter 5).
Decoy
A prank that makes a fake turkey. The next time the farmer would grab a turkey, he grabs the decoy instead (Chapter 6).
Detour
A prank that sends the farmer straight to its zone on his next turn, too busy to search (Chapter 6).
Difficulty
Easy, Standard or Hard: it sets the dog, how far the farmer runs, the Scram target, the clock and the Feathers (Chapter 8).
Dinner Clock
The countdown to Too Late. It moves down 1 at the end of every round, and further when a prank happens (Chapter 6).
Dog
The farm dog (Standard and Hard). It sniffs out turkeys and barks, but never grabs (Chapter 7).
EVENT space
A space on the Dinner Clock that’s a multiple of 4. Landing on or passing one means a farm event (Chapter 6).
Farm event
A d6 roll on the events table whenever the clock lands on or passes a multiple of 4 (Chapter 7).
Feather
A flock token. Spend one after a roll to cancel a gobble from the dice (Chapter 4).
Flock
All the turkeys in the game, played by the players. The flock wins or loses together.
Full urge
Urge 5. Anything that would raise it makes you gobble instead (Chapter 4).
Gobble
A turkey gobbling: from a red 6 (or a 6 on the helper die, for the helper), from a full urge, or on purpose. Its urge goes to 0, and the farmer hears it (Chapter 4).
Gobble for a Friend
Gobble on purpose to turn the farmer’s head away from a Spotted friend (Chapter 3).
Grab
The first step of the farmer’s turn: he grabs a Spotted turkey in his zone, and the game ends (Chapter 7).
Great
A 6 on any white die. The roll works, with a bonus for some actions (Chapter 3).
Helper die
The die of a third color that a friend rolls when Lending you a Wing. A 6 on it makes the friend gobble (Chapter 3).
Hidden
In a hiding spot (Chapter 5).
Hiding spot
A place in a zone where turkeys can hide, with a cover and a room (Chapter 5).
“Huh?” token
A marker for something the farmer heard. He heads for the nearest one and checks its spot (Chapters 5 and 7).
Hunker Down
Stay put, hide if you can, and lower your urge or a friend’s by 2 (Chapter 3).
In the open
In a zone but not in a hiding spot. When the farmer searches the zone he ends in, he spots everyone in the open there (Chapter 5).
Kid
The farmer’s kid (5 or more turkeys). It peeks into spots and yells for Dad, but never grabs (Chapter 7).
Knack
A turkey’s special talent (Chapter 2).
Lend a Wing
A friend in your zone adds a white die to your roll and rolls the helper die; a 6 on it makes the friend gobble. Once per round per turkey (Chapter 3).
Let It Out
Gobble on purpose, to reset your urge or lure the farmer (Chapter 3).
Loud
A prank that puts a “Huh?” token on its zone when it happens (Chapter 6).
Next to
Joined by a path. Zones that touch on the map without a path aren’t next to each other (Chapter 5).
Noisy
A zone that takes a 3+ roll to Sneak into, even when the farmer is far away (Chapter 3).
Open zone
A zone with no hiding spots (Chapter 5).
Path
A way between two zones, shown on the map. You can only Sneak along a path.
Prank
A trick that wastes the farmer’s time. Fill its boxes and the clock jumps (Chapter 6).
Puff Up
Raise your own urge by 1 before a roll for an extra white die. Not at urge 5, and not when you Gobble for a Friend (Chapter 3).
Pull a Prank
Roll to tick a prank’s boxes (Chapters 3 and 6).
Quirk
A turkey’s nervous habit (Chapter 2).
Red dice
The gobble dice: one per point of your urge. Any red 6 is a gobble (Chapter 3).
Room
How many turkeys fit in a hiding spot (Chapter 5).
Round
The turkeys’ turn, the farmer’s turn and the end of the round, in that order (Chapter 3).
Route line
The d6 line in a farm table that says where the farmer (or the dog, or the kid) walks next from a zone (Chapter 7).
Scram
A Spotted turkey’s run for it (Chapter 3).
Search line
The d6 line in a farm table that says which hiding spot the farmer (or the kid) checks in a zone (Chapter 7).
Sneak
Move along a path to the next zone, and hide there if you can (Chapter 3).
Spotted
Seen by the farmer. If he’s in your zone at the start of his next turn, he grabs you, unless a Scram or a Gobble for a Friend works first or the decoy takes your place (Chapter 5).
Storyteller
The person who runs the farmer, the dog, the kid and the farm (Chapter 7).
Target
The number a roll’s highest white die must reach, written like 4+ (Chapter 3).
Too Late
The Dinner Clock at 0. The flock wins at once (Chapter 6).
Urge
How close a turkey is to gobbling, from 0 to 5 (Chapter 4).
White dice
The action dice. Your highest white die decides whether a roll works (Chapter 3).
Works, fails
A roll works when its highest white die is at or above the target, and fails when it isn’t (Chapter 3).
Zone
One area of the farm: the Big Barn, the Duck Pond and so on (Chapter 5).
